column3: The day gives birth.
The first praiser is also called a stranger.
The fool’s vexation is named.
Anger is called a flood without an explicit like.
Close to the Hebrew.
The kisses of the hater are abundant, rather than explicitly deceitful.
The full soul tramples honeycomb.
The man’s place is named, not explicitly home.
The sweetness of his friend is compared with counsel of the soul.
Close to the Hebrew.
An answering word is explicitly named.
The prudent person is singular; the actions are expressed as completed.
The second foreign person is female.
The blessing is expressly reckoned a curse to him.
Close to the Hebrew.
Concealing is the verb; oil meets his right hand.
A man sharpens his neighbor’s face.
Fruit is singular.
Face to face and heart to man are stated without explicit reflecting or true.
Close to the Hebrew.
Testing is not explicitly named.
The fool is pounded among crushed grain.
The face of the flock and directing the heart are the images.
The second clause is a question.
The grass disappears and mountain herbs, not grain, are gathered.
No explicit future verbs of providing occur.
Bread and life are explicitly named.
